review_text:
I've been taking my two dogs here for the last 6 years. I can book appointments easily and conveniently, and I've received good service each time. My experience here has been very positive. Dr. Sood is very thorough in explaining issues, exploring solutions, and my two precious dogs are well cared for here. We've been to the vet a lot this year for various reasons unfortunately, so I've got a bit of experience with coming here. When we had an issue that was too specialized, the referred us out to another pet hospital and overall that was a good experience too.
The staff here is also amazing. Friendly, knowledgeable, and they follow up to make sure my dogs are doing well after our visits. I am lucky to have found a good vet here in Oakland!

I am very disappointed in the treatment I received at Woodminster Vet Hospital.  I had taken my young puppy to them since I picked her up from the breeder in 2025.   Initially all was good however on 3 separate occasions when I received a receipt with my pets name on the first page and a list of vaccinations she received during the visit.  I noted that on the second page in black and white were written instructions for another dog who had sustained an insect bite.  When I contacted the office the first and second times this occurred I was assured that they would take care of removing this false documentation from my pets medical record.   On the third time I noted the same language, I insisted on speaking to the manager and owner to voice my concerns which I had to place in writing two times to actually get it done because they stated  it was just the receipt and that my pets medical record was accurate .   As a health care professional with 46+ years of experience I am concerned about their lack of knowledge and understanding that any and all medical record documentation needs to be accurate.  After finally getting the paperwork amended and talking to the owner who profusely apologized,  I thought everything was resolved. Unfortunately, when I called to make a follow up appointment for my pets routine vaccination on 6/26/26 I was first told they didn't have any available appointments which was untrue because my friend who I recently referred to them made an appointment on the same day.  After thinking about it I called back and was then told that I needed to talk to the coordinator before I could book an appointment and she wasn't in the office and would call me back sometime the following week.   Of note it is now Tuesday 6/30/26 and the office manager has not called me nor sent an email.  

It is now obvious to me that I was banned from the office for making a complaint about a mistake thier office made and no one had the dignity or respect to call me or send a letter so that I can find a new vet for my pet.  

I would not recommend going here as I feel their lack of  integrity and tack which is a big ticket item for me when dealing with anyone who provides care to animals and people, especially when the cost of care is not cheap nor free.

Been here 3 times. The most condescending vet I've ever met and I've been rescuing dogs for over 8 years.  She gives you a hard time, asks to record you?! sends you out of the office then forces her front desk staff to deliver the hard news and the over priced bill. I'm only giving the 2 stars because the two girls at the front were really kind and patient. With so many vets out there these days I do not recommend wasting your money here.

Didn't want to work on my cat because shes aggressive. Wanted to sedate her for blood work. Single vet, busy day. Basically didn't want to deal with her and not sympathetic.

I understand that the staff must be protected.  It was the manner of the vet from the very beginning  which expressed not wanting to do what was needed.  I told her right away that she looked like she didn't want to treat my cat and she didn't refute that.
response_content: The cat is aggressive and hissing at techs. For the safety of our techs, we have to, at times, offer sedation to work on them. We hope you understand the safety of all is important.

review_text: We've been bringing our dog, Tilly, to Woodminster Veterinary Hospital for the past four years and we've consistently had wonderful experiences. Dr. Salwan, Dr. Sood, and the entire team are knowledgeable, compassionate, and attentive. They've been there for routine wellness care, vaccinations, and whenever we've had questions or concerns, always taking the time to explain things clearly and make us feel confident in Tilly's care. Highly recommended!

We've been going to Woodminster for almost 20 years and haven't had any issues till now. It seems like there may be new management? We recently brought our 12 yr old dog in recently with an ear hematoma and were initially quoted a very large sum for a surgery to put a draining port in her ear. After discussion and some not very clear explanation the bill was brought down to $1,500. Then when there was concern expressed to us about her age, her newly diagnosed heart murmur we decided to go with the less invasive drain procedure with medication to address the supposed ear infection for $800 plus some extra medication costs on top of it. We had our doubts about an ear infection and thought her hematoma was more likely due to ear flapping/shaking from the allergies she has. Her ear filled up the next day, and we got a call next business day with few answers. Finally got in touch with the vet who after some garbled explanations referred us to another hospital for the surgery and walked back her explanation that our dog was too old and fragile with heart conditions.  She prescribed more ear drops and pain killers. When we called to see if meds were ready for pickup and add allergy medications to address the underlying problem...we were told we had to pay for another specialist before we could get allergy medications. Mind you we'd already paid for new blood work and this dog had been seen over the years for allergy concerns. Long story short and a whole lot of money later.....we ended up going to another vet, having our dog seen in under an hour for a 10th of the cost, with a vet who clearly cared about our dog's well being, listened to our concerns and explained everything clearly.

I would not recommend going here. I just took my cat in, who is on palliative care at this point, and they did not read his chart. The doctor offered services already rendered and did not know what meds he was on. She stayed in the room with me for all of 2 minutes, told me my cat was constipated and didn't return to tell me what to do next or what my options are for keeping him most comfortable. Staff were short with me when I said I'd been there an hour and a half and had to go back to work, told me the doctor would call me to follow up. By end of day, no call. In the very least, read the notes. This was a very distressing waste of time and money. I am now going to have to see another vet for advice, who can do their job and communicate. Not sure why this place thinks they can operate like this, but this is the last time I will bring any pet there.
They are unresponsive and rude. I would not use them after using them for years they just did not seem to care

A huge waste of time and money, they will worry about what's best for them rather than what is best for your pet. My time, money, and travel was wasted while my pet was not given care. Avoid this godforsaken place at all costs.

I have been going to Woodminster since 2021. I have a 13 yr old Chihuhua Mix, Traviesa, who sometimes needs a muzzle in order to be seen. They have always treated her with kindness and compassion every time we go to her appointments. 
Prices are fair and if you decline any services you don't want done, you can do that without any issue. 
I've never had a communication issue with them. They always follow up after an appointment and they seem to genuinely care for her. Thank you!
response_content:
Took my 13lb Chihuahua mix to get her teeth cleaned here a few months ago. I was a bit nervous because my dog is not the friendliest when she's nervous. We chose to put a muzzle on for safety and they were very kind and accommodating to her and the procedure went well. 
We've taken her a few times now to get several shots and they are always so kind to her Thank you so much.

review_text: I am not a fan of this veterinary clinic having had a truly terrible experience on my first and only visit. My primary complaint is that you are not permitted to accompany your pet during the examination. You are forced to explain the problem to a veterinary technician in the waiting room and then they take your pet back to be examined by the doctor while you remain in the waiting room. Only after the examination are you permitted to meet with the doctor for her consultation. Being separated from your pet and not being present during the examination is a reprehensible protocol. I was informed that my cat was uncooperative and they were unable to do anything while presenting me with a $1000 bill for proposed services.  I refused and left unhappy. Afterwards, I made an appointment with a mobile veterinary service who came to my home and had no difficulty treating my cat. As a new client, I was provided paperwork when I arrived. It included the procedure for the examination. It specified very clearly that I was to remain in the waiting room until the veterinarian examined my pet and then I would be given a consultation regarding her findings.  I was never offered the option to be present during the examination. Beware of veterinarians who bribe clients for five star reviews. I would not recommend this clinic.
response_content: Thank you for your feedback. We're sorry your experience didn't meet your expectations. While many exams are performed in our treatment area to allow our doctors and technicians to work together efficiently and provide thorough care, clients are always welcome to request that the examination be performed in the exam room, and we are happy to accommodate whenever possible. I also reached out privately in an effort to clarify and address your concerns, but you declined further discussion. Should you choose to visit us again in the future, we would be more than happy to have the doctor perform the examination with you present in the room.

review_text: I love taking my baby Mojave here to see the doctor. Last week she an infestation of fleas but we are getting better. She also had an ear infection as well pls pray for us and thank you again. Woodminster

We took our dog to get his updated vacs and his nails clipped and paw assessed for possible infection. We know he is behavioral and properly sedated and muzzled him.

After almost 2 hours of the apt, both waiting for our turn and them "working" with him, the tech told us that they could not even examine his paw nor clip his nails! They were able to draw his blood--a procedure we did not even feel necessary. This also happened to be the most expensive item on the bill. 

How are they able to draw blood and give him injections and not even assess  an infected paw?! They suggested complete sedation for the nail clipping and paw assessment which would cost an additional $550. We left feeling bamboozled and defeated. Looking elsewhere going forward
response_content: We’re truly sorry to hear about your experience. It seems that Kinako bit a technician in December 2022. During the examination, Kinako was sensitive about his paws, and the doctor suggested sedation to more thoroughly evaluate the issue.

I've moved several time with this dog, so she's seen a lot of vets, and Woodminster has been equal to any of them in quality and service. And my dog agrees, she's always happy to go back with the staff, never skittish or reluctant.

Per my initial review, please don't go here if you have other options. I recommend getting on Grand Lake Vet's waitlist or making the drive to the SPCA. My stupid drama aside, Woodminster is objectively bad at what they do from an office efficiency and medical competency standpoint.

response_content:
How many hours have I wasted on Woodminster? The limit does not exist.

Really, though. I would rather get a root canal hanging upside down than ever return here. My brain is short circuiting with rage as I reflect on the inefficiencies and incompetencies of Woodminster Veterinary Hospital. It's quite astounding that they have positive reviews. Let me...let me just lay out some of my experiences in a list:

1) you WILL need to wait 20-30 minutes when you arrive and maybe call the front desk 2-3x to remind them that you're outside, after many many hold times.
2) the vet WILL talk shit about other patients to you. ("you see that black dog out there? your dog isn't that bad, THAT dog is really something")
3)  the vet WILL go on about services that your pet isn't being seen for and probably does not need. One time, the vet insisted that our dog needed a foxtail removed from his ear, ready to charge us hundreds of dollars for this -- without confirming that there actually was one stuck there OR even providing an explanation for why our dog needed this procedure, beyond "we do this all the time." (Spoiler alert: there was no foxtail)
4) honestly, the vet WILL sound drunk sometimes. Very very bizarre and disorganized communication style. I don't honestly think they are drunk, but I don't know whether this makes it better or worse. At the very least, I am convinced they don't review your pet's record at all before speaking with you. 
5) the tech WILL not know how to handle a dog with normal vet reactive behaviors. our 10 lb chihuahua has a warning growl which caused the tech to dramatically drop the anesthesia needle, throw her hands up defensively, and act as though this was a 100 lb dog violently reacting to her. maybe this was her first day on the job. I have never seen a tech or vet overreact to our small, old chihuahua like this. 
6) if you need medical records, they WILL do anything but deliver on this and/or send you the wrong thing. I am with a different vet now and have pet insurance - the pet insurance needs medical records from Woodminster and I think I just need to cancel the insurance because as expected, Woodminster never got back to me after 3 emails about the matter.

To be fair, the front desk staff is always polite and I *think* they are trying their best under the circumstances. They always took on my dogs when no other vet office could make time for them, though I can't help but wonder if the vet services here only exacerbated some of my dogs' problems.

review_text:
I've been using this vet for several years now. They are knowledgeable, good with the animals and straight forward. I had 2 older cats (now both deceased) and the vet helped me through a very difficult time.
My 2 young ones have had the standard care and hopefully will have healthy lives.
I like a neighborhood vet that isn't part  of a huge company. Works for me.

I have been going to Woodminster vet for about 1.5 years now. My dog is a 28 lb mixed breed and he is very nervous at the vet. 

Scheduling: Scheduling is very easy, I call them and there is very rarely a wait time. The whole process takes less than 5 minutes most of the time.

Reminders: They send email and text reminders for appointments, very helpful. 

Care: The team is very caring, everyone has been very patient with my dog. I find the vet to be very knowledgeable about my dog's behavior and health. She also isn't too quick to turn to drug-based interventions (I have heard that some vets will be quick to prescribe something to your pet and miss an opportunity to really dive into the potential issues). 

Accessibility: There is lots of street parking nearby, it is not the most accessible location for public transit. (Typical for east Oakland).

Waiting Room: The waiting room is small but never has more than 1-2 people in it and that has always been easy.

Insurance: They send itemized receipts the day of appointments and that has always made filing claims easy.

Affordability: I used to take my dog to the vet in San Francisco and this is more affordable. They are also understanding and go over their plan with me before acting on it. That way I can choose whether or not I want to defer something like dental cleanings during times when I can't necessarily spare the expense. 

Downsides: The building has thick walls and that means you can't really do work or other things on your phone.

I am highly disappointed with Woodminster  because not only did they mess up once but twice. The first time had been when we brought our Maltese in for cremation. We carried her body in with her bed and favorite blanket. Thinking i would get that back in return with her ashes. But instead they claimed it burned along with her cremation without my consent. What makes you think i would not want those back if was all i had left of her. Was i suppose to drop her body off in a plastic trash bag?? There was no communication and just so insensitive not to follow up if i wanted the items or not. Now fast forward to today. Our second dog passed away and there was two options for cremation private or communal. My brother had taken him and checked off communal cremation thinking private was you get to witness. They didn't explain it vividly that communal you don't get the ashes back. We were all in distress and made the wrong decision. But they're so insensitive that they did not confirm if that's what we forsure wanted after having our dog for 15 years. They even said it would take 3-4 weeks. Why even mention that if i was never going to get his ashes backs. What makes you think i would pay you guys to cremate him. I would've just thrown him in the garbage or beach if so. Overall disappointed in their lack of communication and how insensitive this vet is.
response_content:
Hi Jasun M.,

Your brother signed in the section marked "communal." There is a clear distinction between communal and private cremation. This is the first time we've encountered a situation where the owner was unaware of the difference. While I understand you're grieving, it's not fair to place blame on us. We always make sure to clearly explain the differences. We extend our condolences to you and your family, and we recognize how difficult this is to process, but please understand this is not our fault.

review_text:
The staff works to make sure you're taken care of quickly. The vet is thorough and makes suggestions. Their fees are very reasonable. 

They went the extra mile for me and Bear to have a good experience there.

I was excited to find a vet that had availability that was so close to our house. 

1) What is the point of the intake form if they don't read it? I have a hairless dog and the vet had the nerve to ask me if it had a skin condition and if he would ever grow hair when the intake form stated his hairless breed.

2) The vet told me that if he is drinking too much water that he might have a health problem and that we should test for it...another weird suggestion as puppies drink a ton anyhow (at least ALL OF MINE have before they turned a year old).

3) Every vet has provided me with vitals. That is the first thing that they do when we check in at the vet. Since were in a pandemic, I have not been able to accompany him into the facility. On his last visit, I received no vitals...not even anything as simple as his weight. I even sent two emails and left voice mails....I have yet to receive a reply.

We will not be back. Such a bummer since they've are so close to our home.

I hope they're more thorough with their other patience and clients. We definitely did not get that warm experience that I've been used to with my other animals.
response_content:
Hello MJ L.
Thank you for taking the time to review our practice. Your feedback is very important and we take your concerns seriously. The health of your pet is the highest priority to us, this is why when we saw your dog, a very rare breed to the area, our first observation was the hairlessness, which for dogs that are not Xolo's or Chinese crested etc. would be very concerning. When we saw Sebastien on 5/14/2021 I personally checked him in and knew he was a Xolo right away and had expressed personally how rare it was to see this breed and how well mannered he was, no one had expressed any concern with our check-in process or issues with previous appointments during that time. Also, on the invoices that contain the vaccine information the weight is updated upon every visit. 
 
We are very sorry that you did not have a warm experience here, we pride ourselves in being a neighborhood vet that people having been coming to for years. The COVID curbside experience has made this very difficult on everyone, especially pet owners. If you would like to discuss this further I would be more than happy to chat with you to see if we can rectify this situation. Please ask for Hana. Thank you again, and we hope you're having a wonderful week thus far!

review_text:
The entire team at Woodminster vet is exceptional! They have really taken great of my boy like their own and their treatment plans work! 

Thank you Woodminster vet hospital! Very grateful for your services!

I don't usually feel such a strong need to update a review, but I just can't in good conscience leave a five star review up for this establishment.  When I first came to Woodminster, I was in a bind because my vet retired and I needed immediate care for my dog. The staff offered me a discount for a five star review, which I was happy to do given how friendly they'd been and how easily I got an appointment. I started recommending them to friends and everyone kept giving me the same negative feedback - expensive, not helpful, upselling services, didn't like how my pet was cared for, etc. 

I didn't understand it because my initial visit was good. Unfortunately, the more I went to them, the more I also felt the upselling, but I simply declined the additional services. They got pushier with the upselling and sometimes wouldn't let me decline bloodwork (even though they knew his history and he isn't on any medication). I started coming to them only when absolutely necessary (mostly foxtail removals). Each time I took him in, I left feeling more and more frustrated with the service. This last encounter was the final straw. 

My dog got a foxtail in his ear. I tried calling other vets in the area but nobody could see him. I reluctantly called Woodminster and they got him in for a consult. About an hour later I get a call asking if I know why he's shaking his head so much and if I know when it started?!? "Yes! He has a foxtail in his ear, which is why he's there!" We go through some questions and the tech says I'll get a callback after she consults the Vet. They call me back and quote me $1080 for the removal. Let me start by saying we are active and foxtails (even with the mesh guard worn over the head) are the bane of my existence. My old vet once joked they should name a room in the clinic after one of my dogs because of how often he got foxtails. That said, I have never ever-ever-ever been quoted something so outrageous for a foxtail removal. Not only was that exorbitant, it was outright infuriating because they know we care about our pets and are in a difficult situation. I told them no and said I would come get my dog. I hung up and a couple minutes later I get a call back saying they could do it for $825 if I decline the bloodwork. I tell them no again and that I'm already on my way. I pick him up, get charged for the office visit, and proceed to keep making phone calls. 

THANK GOD for PETS Referral Center in Berkeley!! They are amazing - so incredibly professional and kind, communicative, reasonably priced (they are within the average vet rates for a removal $300-$400), and they service emergency situations. I love them! I will never go back to Woodminster. I didn't realize how bad it had gotten until this comparative experience. 

Note: It's not just about the cost of services, it's also about their overall customer service. They are not an upscale fancy vet.
response_content: I needed same day vaccines for my dog and this was the only place I could get into on such short notice. Not only did they call me back within 15 minutes, but I also got an appointment within the hour on a Saturday. The staff is incredibly friendly, the office is easy to get to, parking can be a little difficult, but the prices are comparable to other vets, so it makes the parking situation negligible. I'm definitely making Woodminster my new vet.

review_text:
SAVE YOUR PET, YOUR TIME, AND YOUR MONEY AND DO NOT GO HERE. The words deceitful and unprofessional describes this establishment. 

I elected to crop my Doberman's ears and had the worst experience here. I unfortunately am not from the area and found them online via yelp (I should have read more of the many one star reviews they have received detailing the same unprofessionalism I experienced). I went through the process of cropping my dogs ears, paid the necessary deposits, had the required tests done, etc. 

I came in for my PLANNED AND SCHEDULED procedure for my dog to have his ears cropped and was told by the office that he was not a candidate as he failed the cuticle bleeding test and he may have V.W. disease... All fine by me as I would never want to put my dog in harms way just to have his ears cropped if something like that was suspected. But, as I went back to the office to get a refund for a procedure he did not have that I had PAID FOR IN FULL, things started to not add up and I was getting the run around from multiple people who clearly do not know what their own office offers procedural wise. 

The way they do their itemizations in their receipts are very deceitful. They itemized everything up pre-procedure so I saw what I "thought" was everything I was paying for, but upon not being able to do the procedure, new things appeared on my bill that previously were not on the original invoice and what I had previously agreed to pay for. For a very expensive procedure I was only getting back 1/3 of what I had paid for, when the procedure itself (that did not happen) cost 2/3 of the bill. Also, they wanted to send me a check in the mail as my refund? If they can take your money that fast but using their tap to pay system, why can they not give it back? Absolutely unacceptable.

Upon questioning why was I getting charged for these new things, one of the staff members that I spoke to (unfortunately I do not have their names) went into defense mode and proceeded to insult me but saying, and I quote "our staff member was with your dog for two hours when they could have been assisting other dogs"... Was this not a service YOU provide and that I had planned and paid for? Why would you offer something that you can not accommodate with staff and time? Our conversations had nothing to do with the care given to my dog, only to why I was being charged what I felt was unfair because there were new things added to my bill that I had not previously seen and seemed unjust. 

I ended up taking less than what I should have gotten back just so that I would never have to go back and see those people again. I should have been given an apology and I do not know why I said that I was sorry to that lady who made the above statement for making them feel that me inquiring about the bill had to do with me demeaning their vet tech work. In no way did what I say about my bill reflect that. So to you, I'm not sorry for what I said, but I'm sorry you feel that way about your clients and your job. It had nothing to do with that. 

IN SUMMARY, go somewhere else. They are deceitful in how they bill you and unprofessional when you question anything that has to do with money.

My family and I bring all three of our dogs to Woodminster and are always happy with how they're treated while there. My dog is super anxious but she loves visiting the vet techs, they treat her to so many cuddles and make her feel at much as ease as possible under the circumstances. Alex in particular is amazing at answering our questions and concerns with patience and giving us helpful tips and recommendations. I highly recommend them due to their incredible staff!

Woodminster doctors and office staff have been caring for my dogs for 8 years. Dr. Adar is caring and thorough as is the staff. It's a great feeling when the the staff know me and my dog and I get know a bit about them as well.
Getting the quarantine protocol was a little rough at first but the new phone system has greatly improved the whole process. 
I highly recommend Woodminster Veterinary.
response_content:
My dog is an absolute angel.  Since July he has been experiencing skin problems.  He had gotten medication that helped him then a month later the problems were back.  I called Woodminster Vet on a Monday morning after a weekend of finding clumps of hair everywhere around the house that he had scratched off.  I felt so bad for him as it was clear how very uncomfortable he was. review_text:
I want to start of this review with the fact that they literally solicit 5 star reviews via email, offering discounted dental cleanings via a raffle, which explains the inflated 4 star rating. This same 4 star rating is what led me to go here. 

We had initial drama which they ended up resolving, we purchased Revolution flea treatment from them for 155 dollars. It didn't work at all, and our cat ended up cutting his chin open because he was so itchy from fleas, and he repeatedly cut himself for the next 3-4 months, as the wound would get itchy during the healing process. We weren't instructed on how to fix the cut, though they did give us cleaning solution. I had to call them 4 days straight, 4 different times, and I did get emotional on the third and fourth call, which led them to actually help, and they refunded the majority of the Revolution. But the service there was alarming, and when you are taking your pet babies to a place, you need/want good service. Also as other reviews have noted, you'll wait at least 30 minutes here each time you come in. 

Their philosophy: they try to charge you for everything they possibly can, without any guidance as far as alternatives, and each charge is surprisingly high.

A vet should be your trusted advisor, but with them I feel like I'm interacting with a con artist. I literally did not trust anyone here at all, from front desk to the vet.

So next time we went in was for our cat to be neutered and he had a breathing issue we wanted them to check. They kept our cat in the office for the entire day for the neuter, and they called us in the afternoon saying they wanted to get the results on the X Ray to diagnose the breathing issue before they neutered our cat (which was fair). We assumed that the vet could read the X Ray, but they had to send it to a radiologist, for an additional $150, so the X Ray cost 400 in total. Then the radiologist I guess says "There is something in his chest, but I'm not sure." What a useful consultation, glad we paid $150 for it. They also kept our cat that day from 9 AM-6:30 pm, so our cat spent 9.5 hours at this Vet for an X Ray.

Then the second day we took him back in for the neuter as I guess the X Ray passed the test (did it tho?). The neutering went fine, I understand it's an incredibly easy procedure. If you look online, this should only cost $50 or so. This placed charged over 600 dollars between blood work, painkillers, anesthetics, and the neuter. Get your cat neutered elsewhere, I promise you'll save a ton of money. 

Also, they described our other cat as fractious (vet word for mean or pain in the butt) multiple times and said your other cat is so nice unlike this cat. I literally told them this cat was rehabbed at a center for cats that have lived terrible lives, a lovely local place called Cat Town, but that didn't stop them from talking smack about my cat. The lady was lucky I was patient with her on that. 

And for my other cat who they said is so sweet, any time he got a vaccine shot or any shot from them, the wound was always quite bloody, while our other cat (the "fractious" one) who once went to emergency room had gotten multiple shots with 0 blood. I think they were rough with our cat, but they do everything behind closed doors (COVID Policy that was still in place late 2022 after COVID was declared a non-issue). I think this policy is in place because it ensures people cannot see what they do to our pets. 

Long story short: I don't trust this place at all, they seem to be eager to charge you for anything and everything. They hold your pets there way too long as they overbook, which leads to you waiting 30 minutes every time you go in for your pet. Their bedside manner is poor, as they will insult your pet to your face, and not return your calls. You'll get little to no advice unless you ask tons of questions, but as a pet owner you need prescriptive information. I wouldn't go here unless you have 0 choices. Our cat's breathing issue remains unresolved, but luckily we moved out of the East Bay. Adios Woodminster!!!

** Extremely disappointing pet care for BOTH cats **

I hate writing negative reviews, but I need to share my experience with other devoted pet owners. I have taken my 2 young cats to Woodminster for care since I adopted them in 2020. I have spends $1000s of dollars on both preventative care & diagnostic tests. 

One of my cats, at just 2 years old, was diagnosed with kidney failure, and I could not be more DISGUSTED with the utter lack of communication, compassion, follow up & support from Woodminster. 

After spending WEEKs trying to figure out how to get an urgent diagnostic ultrasound (Woodminster EVENTUALLY did the test), I literally had to call 8 times & break down in tears on the phone to get someone to call me back to discuss the results & possible next steps for my suffering cat. 

Net-net, my cat was dying. But they couldn't say anything more about... What stage of kidney failure? How long will he last? How will I know when he's suffering?

When it became clear that my dear cat was indeed suffering & needed to be euthanized, Woodminster told me they "weren't sure when they would be able to get us in" for this urgent care. 

I ended up having to call every vet & emergency vet hospital in the area to find immediate support. It was one of the worst experiences of my life, hearing my cat howling in pain & see him unable to stand... all while no one at Woodminster could/would help. 

They still don't know that he's now dead as they've never followed up to ask what I ended up doing when they couldn't help me euthanize him. 

Unbelievably, while this saga was unfolding, my SECOND young cat started having severe coughing/ choking/ vomiting fits multiple times each day. I brought him into Woodminster for chest X-rays & bloodwork, paid $1000s again, and was sent home w 2 Rx's that did nothing to help. 

Again, no one from Woodminster EVER called to follow up or  schedule a follow up appt to figure this out. He continued to suffer, getting worse every day. 

I found another vet who immediately went into action. She was horrified watching my young cat struggling for every breath, said he was in very bad shape & she needed to URGENTLY see the X-rays and blood work results from Woodminster. 

Not only did Woodminster never share those results with me... they WOULD NOT send the results to me or my new vet after we called MANY times over multiple days... we were told that the records couldn't be shared because there was no vet on duty at the time.

The new vet did an immediately ultrasound & bloodwork, trying to understand what was causing my cat's distress. This vet didn't have X-ray equipment on site, so it would take a day or 2 to get new X-rays done offsite. We immediately started treating the breathing issues w strong steroids & antibiotics, which quickly provided relief. This vet has called me MULTIPLE times to check in, offer add'l suggestions & support, and ensure that my cat is recovering. 

Again, there has been ZERO follow up or concern from Woodminster for either of my cats. They must be too busy ...
because I simply can't believe that they have such little regard for the animals & owners that trust them to provide care.

UPDATE: On the day I posted this review, I received a voicemail from Woodminster, asking about my cat, Cole. I have not returned their call.

This review is from my experiences prior to the COVID 19 pandemic and business shutdown. 

This place definitely does the up-"sale"-ing thing. Their prices are moderately above average. But it's the way they recommend, firmly sometimes, the most expensive care plan. It's a lot of "it could be something more serious" and not a lot of laying out the possibilities with probabilities. 

I experienced this when my dog had a stomach virus and upon examination, the vet went straight for doing a variety of labs and tests, estimating towards a grand. Thinking that there were huge red flags I heavily contemplated going this route. Sprinkle in the vet saying "it could be serious" and looking somber, I almost did. 

Thankfully I second guessed this place because Iayed out the same symptoms list to a friend of a friend (vet) and a different local business that's also a vet hospital, and the recommended plans were so different. The recommendations weren't influenced by me either because all I talked about was my dog's symptoms not what a previous vet recommended. 

Another issue I had was the general inconsistency of the front desk. Some staff were helpful (I will not deny) but some were often confused and negligent. One staff checking me out neglected to tell me the first administration of the influenza vaccine had to be followed up with a second shot three weeks later. At our appointment (months later) she said I never came back for the second appointment so we had to start over with the first of two shots administering the influenza vaccine. I said I was never told this when checking out or during my visit ever. She didn't really have much of a response so I had to schedule a third (potentially avoidable) visit for the shot. And pay for it. Looking back, I wish I would have been more firm about this issue. I kind of just let it go but it was one of many layers that bothers me about this place. 

Some other minor things: wait times are unnecessarily long (vaccine appointments turn into 1.5-2 hour trips. 95% of which is you waiting in a room. Vaccines always left sizable bumps on my dogs and had them shy ("they're not shy") and lethargic for several days. I thought all that was normal...

Vets are one of those things that you don't realize you have it bad or good until you move on to a different thing. In this case, I had it bad and didn't realize until I switched vets. It was the front desk mistake over the influenza vaccine that got me to switch. Once at a different vet, the up sale-ing and the mistakes from the front desk disappeared. My new vet even questioned some of the optional vaccines my dogs had gotten (strongly recommended by this vet here) saying that my dogs were very low low risk. 

Almost every visit here was a negative experience for me. And if that was too long for you to read, here's the short version:

-recommends most pricey treatment plan without weighing options
-inconsistent front desk staff (1-2 which are, to me, incompetent. Hate saying that because it's mean)
-insane wait times

If you go here and want the name of another local vet that is much better, please private message me. Your life will improve.

For being a small place, it's really very accommodating and able to take my dog within the week and even sooner if it's extra concerning like when he had a terrible ear ache. The front desk people are helpful and kind, and never make me feel bad for missing their numerous calls or forgetting something. And vet techs are always kind to my little dog even though I know he's a reactive little devil who resists any little thing, and they never treat him differently. The doctors also explain stuff well and never fear monger in order to make more money. 

Overall a really great place for a mid 20s person like me who doesn't have an endless amount of money to spend on her doggie but will do anything for her bb!

It's been a few years, so I felt the need to post an update! Forever grateful for Woodminster and how amazing they are. A couple years ago, they were so thoughtful to call me to see if I could emergency foster a pup who belonged to a client of theirs who were no longer able to keep her. While many vet clinics take amazing care of their patients, few go as far to help network for dogs who need fosters, training, and support their clients as a whole past the scope of the veterinary services they provide. I was floored that the staff cared so much about this dog that they wanted to make sure she landed in a loving home.

It ended up working out and we decided to keep her! When she unfortunately developed a tumor more recently, Woodminster was able to find us a next day appointment for x rays and to aspirate the lump. Throughout the cancer diagnosis, Woodminster helped us every step of the way in any appointments or medications needed, helping us find an oncologist, checking in on us to see how things were doing, and helping us figure out which path was best for our sweet Nasa. 

Thank you, Woodminster, for being so compassionate and always going above and beyond, even throughout this pandemic and how hectic things have been this last year.

Gave our puppy a vaccine the breeder had specifically said not to do so until 8 months old. I told the vet at the first visit and showed them the list of things not to give, but they gave it anyway!

And then very confidently lectured me on how their mistake was simply the law and their vet school educations triumphs anything apparently ignorant breeder told me. Even if it's the law, I believe my consent is still needed for any vaccination that I had said NOT to give.

Edit: my partner DID NOT AGREE to the Rabies Vaccine. By "Consent", what they meant was they THINK they said it and they THINK he allegedly heard it, but he did not say okay nor did he acknowledged anything. He actually had to correct them twice what vaccine he was getting and specifically said "HPPV ONLY". The miscommunication is this vet NOT HEARING what we said, but only claiming to hear what she apparently claimed to have said but was never acknowledged. We also shared the list of vaccines he should NOT GET at the first visit - in bold RED print in WRITING and also verbally. 
While I understand it is the law, the law is for puppies at 5 months old, this puppy is not even 4 months!

I spoke with the breeder who now says this is extremely bad and she will no longer guarantee the health of her dogs. We now have to watch over the dog 24/7 for any adverse reactions for the next 4 days. And this ridiculously vet chalks it up to "a bad communication". The fact that they tried to deny any responsibility by insisting my partner had verbally consented to it (when he did not) and then argue it is by law and therefore they had the right to do it is beyond ridiculous.

The "law" as they claim is here:
California law requires each dog older than three months to be vaccinated against rabies and licensed before it is five months old. If your dog is more than five months old, you have 30 days to get it licensed after you obtain it or bring it into California.
response_content:
Hello Charissa O.
Your Partner, who brought Joey in today without you, did consent to giving him the Rabies vaccine.  Two staff members were present when this happened. We apologize if there was a miscommunication about this situation between you and your partner. When it comes to required dog vaccinations in California, the only mandatory one is the rabies vaccine. State law dictates that dogs older than three months old must receive the rabies vaccine. For the health and safety of your pet, all of the other pets in our hospital and our staff we are not willing to break the law, that would not only be irresponsible but illegal and we would hope you would want other pet owners to be just as responsible. Thank you for your understanding and have wonderful weekend. 

- Hana

Edit: There is no "HPPV" vaccine for canines, I believe you are referring to DHPP. We were given consent to vaccinate for DHPP and Rabies today, there were two technicians present while this was authorized.   Below I have included the California law, or penal code as it relates to rabies. 

"Dogs shall be considered to be properly vaccinated for the purposes of section 121690, California Health and Safety Code, when injected at three months of age or older with an approved canine rabies vaccine."

http://publichealth.lacounty.gov/vet/docs/CARabiesLawsandRegulations2014-2606.pdf

review_text:
Overall, we have had a positive experience at Woodminster for both our cat and dog. The staff is friendly, the office is easy to get to, and the vets have good communication skills.

review_text: I really like Woodminister Veterinary Hospital. They are quick to reply to calls or emails and have handled my two cats very well. One of my cats had very slightly kidney levels and they were very clear in explaining how to care for her, what food to get, and the plan for the future. The positives:

After speaking with the veterinarian on site that day we felt comfortable moving forward with the surgery. My cat was awake when I went to pick him up and he looked completely relaxed, despite being drowsy from the sedation, he was not upset and looked at peace during the whole consultation,drop off and pick up process. Earlier today I also received a follow up phone call to check on how my cat is doing. Excellent patient care!

Would hands down recommend this facility to all my fellow fur-parents, I will definitely come back if needed in the future. The Only down side is that traffic is Horrible going back to San Francisco, so plan your time accordingly.  Thanks to Woodminster Vet, Luffy is recovering perfectly!!

review_text:
My dog has been a patient of this veterinary hospital for over 4 years, and up until March, we liked coming here. He seemed comfortable with the techs and doctors and they seemed to like him in return. Last December (2020), I tried to make an appt for his rabies shot and was told that I'd have to wait until the end of January for an appt. I agreed because it was just a routine shot appt and they told me that it would be okay if it was a little bit overdue. As I'm on the phone finalizing his routine rabies shot appointment, I asked what would happen if my dog became sick during the pandemic (because of the LONG wait time to get a shot).  They said they had appointments available if the dog were to become sick. 

At the beginning of March (2021), he became sick, extremely lethargic, and stopped eating. I knew I had to take him in to be treated. I called the office to get an appt and they told me they didn't have an appt until the end of April. I was outraged that they didn't have any appts available to treat sick pets. They told me to call around to see if I could take him to another vet clinic in the meantime. Of course, because of COVID, no one had availability or were taking new patients. I understood because he didn't belong to another clinic, he was a patient of Woodminster (which should have treated him). I ended up at VCA Emergency Pet Hospital in San Leandro and he was treated. Thank goodness for the help from VCA, if they wouldn't have treated him, he would have probably died. 

At the end of March, I needed to have his Trifexis medication refilled and I had to call them to pick it up. When I went to pick up the Trifexis, I made a comment to the tech who brought out the Trifexis to me about their poor service to treat one of their patients. She then mentioned to me that they were completely booked up with dental cleaning appointments. I think it's unbelievable that they wouldn't have emergency appointments available for sick pets. This clinic is just out to get your money and they don't really care about your pet. DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME bringing your dog or cat here.
response_content:
Hello Rosa D.

I am so sorry to hear about what happened. Would you be able to give me a call so I can look into this situation further? During COVID we are only able to have a certain amount of people in the building and we had to put off urgent dental appointments for one year. If we are not able to get a pet in right away we always refer to the closest ER Vet so that your pet does not have to wait to be seen. Again, if you are able, please call and ask for Hana, as I would like to investigate this situation further. Thank you, and hope you are having a great week thus far!

review_text:
Been a loyal customer to this place for years, they were great then. They've treated all my babies even when we needed surgery they helped us. But recently things have changed. 

My dog has been having intestinal issues and when I called, I was so grateful they could take me in the same day. But it's been 3 days since his X-ray was taken and still I have no results. It takes two minutes to read an X-ray. They are aware that my dog is not eating and he has not been having bowel movements. On top of that they are fully aware that he has been vomiting. Isn't this a serious matter?? I was told results take 24-48hrs but we are literally going on 72hrs. This place needs to work more on a timely manner. 

Also, he had a blood test and I got results to that but I am the one needing to constantly call and ask about it. Not once did they think it was urgent for me to know and contact me. 

With my last dog, after she passed they called and asked about her, which was great, but when I informed them we had to put her down, the reply I got was "oh you didn't bring her to us to do it?" How insensitive can you be?! I just lost my dog and you're worried I didn't go to you to pay you to do it??? -- we put her down on a Sunday meaning they weren't open anyways. 

This place has gone downhill, please be aware that you should not take your pets here for an urgent matter. They also take over a month to issue refunds for their mistakes.

The front staff are just doing their job the best they can during a pandemic, I understand that. It's just a terrible system, terrible communication, and a terrible vet. My poor dog is traumatized as am I. I'll never go here or recommend this hospital.
I drove a long way to take my dog to them for dental care and was very impressed with the staff and expert care he received. It was well worth the drive!

Woodminster is very convenient for us as we only live 5 minutes away and they have friendly staff.

I took my puppy Feliz here for a diagnoses of mange. We got her the prescription and within a couple of weeks her fur and skin were back to normal!

They treated her with kindness and love, the staff was very helpful.

4/26/17 I received a call from one of the managers apologizing for our experience and refunding the emergency vet cost. Hopefully after his ears are healed and they're symmetrical, I might bump them up to a 3. Bumped them up to 2 stars. I appreciate the follow up (and refund for the emergency visit)! Thank you for your concern,

5/3/17 Got another call from one of the managers following up on how my puppy was doing. PLEASE DO NOT SEND THREATENING EMAILS TO THE OFFICE. They are just trying to do their jobs.

There are not a lot of options for us to get our dogs ears cropped. Elective surgery for dogs: It may sound odd, but have long been routine in certain breeds like Dobermans, German shorthaired pointers, and schnauzers. It is a personal choice and one should not be judged for deciding to crop their dogs ears. Have a professional perform the procedure vs. doing it yourself? Go to the professional! response_content:
Got my dobe's ears cropped. Dropped him off at 10:30am (appointment time). I didn't meet the doctor. There were a lot of young girls in the front office. Some you could tell were training. I left and went about my day. I was feeling a little apprehensive about my puppy's first surgery, but I was a reassuring myself that everything was going to go well since I personally knew someone who went there to get her dobe's ears cropped.

I expected to pick him up at 5:30pm but was pleasantly surprised that I received a phone call that I could pick him up at 4:30pm. (They didn't leave the compression wrap on long enough)

Since he was still sedated, my husband and I ran to the store to buy stuff for him. When we came back, his bandages were off and there was blood in the crate and all over his e-collar. I re-wrapped his ears and he kept shaking his head. There was blood all over the kitchen. My son came home and saw the bloody mess. My daughter came home and freaked out when she saw all the blood. We ended up going to the emergency pet clinic and stayed there from 10:30pm - 1:30am to get his ears re-wrapped properly. More money down the drain.

Lesson learned: meet the doctor who's going to do the surgery and make sure the bandages aren't done by a rookie!!

I give them one star for the trauma my family went through. We were totally unprepared for what transpired this evening.

review_text:
I like the reception staff. They are competent and friendly. My elderly dog went in there with a minor ear complaint. We waited for an hour and a half the first visit and one hour for the follow up. The vet Dr Adar will up sell every invasive treatment there is, without regard to the age or well-being of the pet. It was like going in for a haircut and leaving with heart surgery or something. Without being able to go inside and advocate for my pet, 1400 dollars later, my dog walked out of there shaking, with a cone on her head for no reason. A few weeks later, my dog refused go back inside for the follow up visit. She never acts like that. Bad experience.
I switched veterinarians, and called Woodminster to get my dogs records sent to the new vet. I called twice, and my new vet called twice. Each time the receptionist promised she would give the message to the doctor. The doctor never shared my dogs medical records, although it is their legal obligation  to do so. 
They used to be good, now, sorry to say, I think they are jerks.

I love this pet clinic. I feel confident that my cats are getting the best care. Their new system for keeping exams and shots up to date seems to be working well. Woodminster saved my bad kitty's life when she  got in a fight which turned into a serious infection. 
I feel at home at Woodminster. They are warm caring people.

Long over due review. I've been going here for as long as I can remember for my two boys Halo and Henny. Im local so this is close to home. I have a big Pitbull Halo and a little nugget Frenchie Henny. They've been going here since they were puppies. Staff and everyone is super friendly. They all know and remembers the boys and loves them. Anytime I have to leave the boys there for anything I know I'm in good hands. Never had a problem. Would def recommend if in the area.

I know you can't put a price on the love you have for you companion (dog, cat, etc) However there is a huge difference between paying what's a fare price and being swindled! I rescued a dog a few weeks ago,  I found her alone under a dumpster. I didn't have any information and history on her. I tried clipping her nails on my own, because I got her in the beginning of the pandemic and most grooming places were still closed. I got most of them but unfortunately there was one I couldn't get to. After about a week or so they nail became ingrown. I figured it would be best to take her to a vet. I called Woodminster and I got a quote over the phone. They quoted me the most I would pay would be $250 (this was supposed to include $55 visit, $25 to cut the nails, $40-90 for sedation, and $17 rabies shot and maybe $40 for antibiotics) when we showed up for our appointment we waited over half an hour for one of the assistance to come get our girl. She was in the back for about 30 minutes when the assistant showed up with an estimate ledger quoting $807.06!!!! My Goodness!!!! $807.06 to remove an ingrown nail! Now they wanted to charge me this because they insisted on putting her to sleep to do the procedure. They said my dog wasn't easy to work with, my 15 lb dog wasn't being nice. To sedation was $155.63 and they up the price to cut the nail to $175.00!!!! We went from $25 to cut the nail to $175! After talking to the assistant about the price we were quoted and letting her hear the voicemail that was left my Reina two days before she said she would talk to the veterinarian about doing it for that price. She didn't agree to do it, since we already had to pay $55 for the visit we decided to get some shots that she needed! They gave me a receipt for the visits but didn't want to provide immunization records. What?! How?! So I pressed for them to give me the immunization records. Finally after waiting 30 more minutes they finally gave me the records. I asked for a prescription for a sedative to help my dog, but both of the veterinarians on shift refused to give one to me saying that they didn't feel comfortable! Oh but you feel comfortable charging me $807 to cut a nail?! I feel lied and lured to come here with fake quotes and estimates. I do not believe in my heart that anyone on shift that day truly cares for the well being of my pup! After being at Woodminster for over 3 1/2 hours, I left with a $100 less and a pup that still needed help! I found a dog groomer, who charged me $5 and Took care of the nail in less than two minutes. It saddens me that something that could've been done in two minutes was dangled over my head and was gonna cost me $807. The veterinarian on shift was Dr Adar and Dr Salwan. I am going to move forward on contact the veterinarian board.  This establishment needs to be looked into. Moral of the story don't bring your companions here, these people have no compassion for animals!!!!! None!!!!

review_text: I would like to say prior to taking the drive from Stockton to Oakland (about an hour) I was very hesitant based on a few negative reviews I seen on Yelp. However I stuck with my gut and Decided to give them a chance to see how my own experience would be. I took my 13 week old puppy in yesterday to get his ears cropped to which they did an amazing job. This isn't my first time having a dog get their ear cropped since I own both Dobermans and Bully's. When I went in they were very professional, they took Apollo to the back and took over from there. My main reason for driving to Oakland to begin with is due to my original vet being booked up and not being able to take him in before he reached over 25lbs. After they took Apollo to the back they brought out the papers for me to review and agree to certain treatments that the suggest. Since this isn't my first time I was able to deny several extras that I didn't necessarily find necessary but I do not view it as them trying to "upcharge" me. It is the team being cautious and making sure your pet has the best experience and also being vigilant to be sure nothing goes wrong during the procedure. Since ear cropping is a surgery and the puppy has to be sedated there's a few tests that they SUGGEST for the overall well-being of your pup. Even though I denied these extra tests I did not view it as them trying to push it on me or force me to pay for anything extra. As I said since this isn't my first time, I knew what I would be paying for and what I wouldn't be. For those who are new and it's their first time I can see why they'd feel as if they were being charged more however it is ultimately our choice as the customer to deny what we don't want. I believe the staff did an amazing job both at drop off and at pick up, explaining everything I was receiving and what I would need to do as care for his ears. I would definitely go back to them for my next puppy who's ears need to be cropped. Overall 5/5. Thank you guys! Apollo looks great!

I said can't you just give her a little shot of lidocaine and some stitches?  She said, "Oh no."  I knew this was not true so I asked for an estimate. 
The tech came back with a bill around $800. I said no f--ing way and said I would get my friend to sew it up. 
At least they gave me antibiotics and I left. I called my neighbor (who is a doctor) and she gave her a tiny poke of lidocaine and three stitches. Not one flinch from my dog and all it cost was dinner for my friend. 
To NOT do what was best for my animal made me more upset than wanting to bleed my bank account dry.  Shame on you Woodminster Vet. I hope people read this and not get ripped off just because you want to make a buck.

We were referred to Woodminster from the breeder we got our Cane Corso from. We had been researching ear cropping for over 3 months. Our female was currently 5 months old. We love and adore her nothing was wrong with her but I am a breeder myself and stay true to the standard of the rabbit breed that we bred. We love her ears, I do raise lop earred bunnies. They say unless you are 100% sure don't do it. After much research we made the appointment and followed the pre-op instructions. When went here based on reviews and of course the referral. I had searched and searched for the crop that we feel is best for her. I had found a picture that I continually was draw too and thought was clean and healed nicely which was on a 5 month old cane corso as well. But we came here about an hour drive but worth it. 

We went into the room and the tech asked us if we had questions, of course our family member was going in for a procedure that is permanent and effects the way people would view her. I had to ask twice and third time was the charm for the doctor that was going to do the procedure to come in and talk to is and show us the crop style. 

When the doctor came in, I am so sorry I don't remember her name because she is definitely professional and helped us make a lifelong decision. She was an middle aged Indian lady and very well spoken. She told us without a hesitation that she has no problem doing the procedure and of course vets want the business. She explained it's not hard in her to do the crop being that our corso was 5 months old but it's the bleeding and the pain that our dog would be in that we needed to think about. She was older and we have no problem doing the consistent thorough recovery to make sure everything healed. But she said if we were not 100% sure to not do it. 

5 stars for her and her alone!! Honest and professional!! 

***Note by no means am I against or for ear cropping. Our corso has her tailed docked. I love the breed no matter what. But unfortunately they do get labeled. I firmly believe if your a breeder of anything to bred strictly to the breed standard. If your a pet owner research before committing to a procedure.

I would not go back to this vet because I brought a stray cat in that literally came up to me on a street, and the poor thing had large lymph nodes on both sides of her neck ,that I could see as she came down the sidewalk toward me. I had never seen this sweet cat before. 

I took her to Woodminster to essentially find out if she needed to be euthanized because she was ill. The vet did labs and put a needle in one of the enlarged lymph nodes to get a biopsy, or evaluate the cells. 

When I went back to get results the next day, the vet said that anytime you have such large lymph nodes in a pet, it usually lymphoma, which sounds as though putting a needle in the nodes and getting labs were unnecessary expenses for me. She was a stray and she wasn't going to recover, ever. 

The vet prescribed trazadone for sleep for the cat that first night while I took her home overnight until the results came in. That med is worthless. It does nothing. I've had experience with Trazadone as some doctors used to prescribe it for sleep. It does nothing. My strong opinion is that it is a useless drug and a waste of money. Other vets give generic Gabapentin for anxiety and for sleep. It works. Cat rescue groups routinely use generic Gabapentin to mildly sedate feral cats before they are taken to a vet for eval or procedures. Vets use it to help sedate extremely anxious pets before they examine them. They don't use Trazadone. It doesn't calm the animal or help them sleep. So the cat likely had lymphoma and was going to die, even though she was hungry, had an appetite, and was going to live for several months at most. When I opted to have her euthanized while I stayed with her during the procedure, I was advised it would be about $400.00. My impression was that that was the fee I would be charged. Then, a few minutes later, the vet assistant told me that I could add a sedation injection before she was euthanized in order to make her more comfortable during the procedure. I thought we had settled the cost of euthanasia and now there was an extra sedation injection I could add, for an additional fee. I have never had a vet office give the sedation injection as an additional fee. It's a standard part of the procedure so that the animal doesn't go into distressing seizures and upset the pet owner. 

I advise this vet to stop using Trazadone. Other clients came in while I was in the waiting room, and stated that Trazadone didn't help their pet for restlessness or anxiety at all. Also, give the client the cost of euthanasia and don't add extra charges after you have already advised them of the fee!

Don't give pets a useless medication that doesn't work The pet suffers in the process. It isn't right! I'm not going back. The trust isn't there. 

Stop giving Trazadone. Gabapentin works.

Wow! I've never been let down by this awesome , accommodating crew. 
Got a German Shepard puppy in their care, who broke her leg jumping from my truck. They're the best yet. Hannah, Rachel, Melissa and Dr. Darr has been my favorite by far. Thank you to your amazing staff for always helping me out.

Been bringing our pug here for years. he loves the vet techs as well as the vets. Plenty of street parking (it's usually a sleepy neighborhood) and a few reserved spots for customers across the street.

Our pup is currently on a special diet and they helped us buy ordering the food for us pretty regular; changing his diet has fixed the big issue he was having, so that's been a big relief.
Chato says THANK YOU!
My dog had an ear infection and they did the BEST job of cleaning his ears and providing him with the care he needed! I highly recommend them!

I brought my Louie to Woodminster Veterinary because he was experiencing really bad allergies, a lot of licking at the paws, running eyes etc...Coming into the office it was very friendly & Warm the veterinarian took her time with communicating with us about Louie symptoms and what we can do to try in prevent his allergies, we we're recommended to do blood work and providing Louie with steroids, the steroids worked for a while but eventually his symptoms came back. We took both our boys (pitt mixes) here for initial exams and are in the process of getting their broken teeth extracted. They've been so helpful and accommodating. It's good to feel like they really care about you. Thank you! :)

The staff at Woodminster are great! They were able to help take care of my dogs needs on the "Spot!"
The doctor was great too. The consultation was very in depth and my dog was very much relaxed and well cared for. Although the place may not be warm and "fuzzy" inside, it is very clean and doesn't smell like a pet store.

I wouldnt even rate this vet a star, but to write the review I had to. This place is a totallll SCAM. My puppy came to get her tail docked and the staff and dr were so nice, put me st ease to know my Chloe in good hands. 2015

Avoid at all costs - extremely incompetent and as other reviews mention, they do not care about your animals.  I came in to have my dog checked out for excessive scratching (she had scratched a patch of fur off of her back). They asked to do a skin test on the area that was scratched and indicated it would be 30m. Came back in 30m and they told me she's still not ready - "it will only be another 30m." 30m later, still not ready! Finally after almost 2 hours, she was ready to be picked up. I asked about the results of the test and if it could be allergies, and I got a blank stare from the nurse. Eventually, I got a bogus response that didn't even answer my question (they clearly had no idea what they were talking about). Overall, it was a horrible experience at the vet during my visit and here's an example of the true incompetence of this place:

I called back recently to have an airline form filled out by the vet, indicating my dog was checked out by the vet (the vet filled out almost the exact same form for me the day of our exam for a different airline). Initially, they told me it would be "no problem" and to "just send the form via email and they'll have it filled out and sent back ASAP." After 5 emails, and almost daily calls for 2 weeks, I was told THE DAY BEFORE I NEEDED THE FORM, that they couldn't fill it out ...the dog needed to be examined within 10 days in order to complete the form. Day after day of calling, I kept getting the same answer - "we're working on it and will get it to you." Now it's too late and my dog will not be able to travel with me. Complete incompetence from the entire staff at Woodminster. If I could give zero stars I absolutely would. Avoid this place -- plenty of better vets out there.

When one of my two dear bunnies recently had a serious sudden health issue on a Monday morning and I called Chabot Veterinary Hospital to see if Dr. Harvey was available for an emergency visit, and having been told she wouldn't be in until Wednesday, I was forced to go online and look for a vet who would be able to see her IMMEDIATELY.  I was panicked, scared, and afraid I'd lose her while trying to find someone.  I called Woodminster and a very kind and empathetic woman reassured me that their bunny doctor was in at 10AM and that we could come in right then and she would be seen immediately.  I also had to admit this was at a financially difficult time for me, and she said they'd find a way to work with me to keep the costs down as much as possible.  

They called Chabot Vet and had Hershey's medical records e-mailed up to Woodminster to look at her past history, and I think this is absolutely proactive veterinary care to keep the chain of med records linked carefully.  They then took care of her emergency needs by referring to her past history as a guide to how she recovered a few years ago from this same thing.  

When I got there, the bunny vet was there and ready to see Hershey.  She was to the point and not that folksy, but I was there for medical care, not a social visit.  She gave me a sort of "worst-case scenario" of what could be the problem but said they would look at everything and thought they would be able to take care of her in the outpatient visit.  An hour later, they came out with Hershey and she had been examined, treated, shaved, injected with antibiotics and pain meds, and treated with love and care.  Hershey looked ready to go home, alert and didn't seem to be in a panic from the vet visit, which bunnies can sometimes be affected by.  I got her home and she rested most of the day with her boy, Dude, and he took good care of her by grooming her and nuzzling her all day.  

The cost of the emergency visit including all services was much less than I expected to pay for an emergency visit.  I got expert advice regarding home care and medication administration, and was asked to bring her back the next day to leave her for all-day IV subcutaneous fluids.  I said I couldn't afford much more and was surprised to hear that her all-day fluid hospitalization was only $20.  I dropped her off in the morning and picked her up in the afternoon, and she was happy, healthy, bouncy and not nervous at all.  She got great care.  

Of course, I'll still prefer to take her to Dr. Harvey at Chabot because she IS Hershey's vet (and my all-time favorite vet), but when Dr. Harvey isn't available, Woodminster is my absolute back-up plan.  

They even called me the next day to check on Hershey's well-being, called the following week to again check on her, and I'll always remember those caring follow-ups as proof that this staff and vets do care for the animals they treat.

This place gets four stars for the staff. They are always friendly and they genuinely care about the business (they ask for customer feedback all the time). They're good with animals and they know what they're doing.

If you're looking for cheap, this is your place. Vaccinations, boarding, exams, surgery... they do it all for cheaper than the next guy (except PetVet, which will vaccinate for a few dollars less). 

Word for the potential boarder: animals stay in large boxes and receive two walks a day.
We continue to bring our two Siamese cats to Woodminster. We love the fact that we can get in on an urgent call swiftly. And, the vets here are caring and understand our pets are our everything.
response_content:
We've enjoyed the service and attention at Woodminster. It's hard to feel totally serviced at a vet - I've not been in love with all of them. The entire industry needs to re-think the approach to value for investment of it's customers. I think Woodminster has this in mind and tries more than most. 

We have 2 male cats and they are always very respectful and attentive when I bring them in. review_text:
Everyone I dealt with at Woodminster was very professional and attentive. They seem to have done a lot to adapt to the current Covid reality, and it shows. To be honest, they aren't even my regular vet, but when one of our cats needed to be seen on short notice and our regular vet was booked, Woodminster had an opening. It's several pages long and fairly dense, but when I spoke to the veterinarian she had clearly read it all before tending to our pet. Besides this, and excellent care, we received two follow up calls across the week to check in on our pet.

All of this is to say, I would recommend Woodminster to anyone without any reservations. Your pet will be in good hands here.

I really wanted to love this place, their prices are the most affordable around but because of my last experience here I can say I will NEVER be back here nor do I recommend anyone trusting anything other then regular shots here.

I had paid for the puppy plan with them which is the reason I believe that they didn't really care at all about my last visit. I went in because he needed his last round of shots, and also a check up because his skin had recently started rashing up. Upon arrival I checked in then about 15 minutes later they took my dog to the back for him "check up" and shots. I know for a fact they had left him alone over 30 minutes because I can hear my puppy crying and barking from the waiting room.

I told them about his rashes and told them I thought it was hot spots but that I really wasn't sure at all, that's what the doctor there is for anyways. So after waiting an hour one of the receptionist girls came out to say it was hot spots and that we needed to use some hot spot apart that contained steroids in it to help the hot spots heal I should have known better for the simple fact the doctor herself didn't even bother to come out to talk to us AT ALL. Oh but how wrong they were. After going home and applying the spray in him, after 2 days it got noticeable worst. So i made the decision to take him to an old vet in the city I use to live in that's about 40 minutes away to get a second opinion from a vet a really trusted and had seen for 9 years before transferring over which I had only decided because I moved to Oakland and it was more convenient for me. 

Thank god I did so because they had actually discovered that it wasn't hot spots but actually mange, and the mediation this place recommend 
 it only made it worse because of the steroids the spray contained makes mange spread more aggressively.. Oh this place also missed the fact that the mange had cause BOTH ears to have infection. What a freaking joke this place is!

If you plan on taking any of your pets here because of any issue other than shots I recommended you DON'T

DO NOT GO TO THIS VET!

On May 11th 2011 our beautiful  border collie Max who loved everyone and was only 9 and was what amounts to being killed because of neglect while being boarded at Woodminster.                                                         

He was there for only 3 days and when we went to pick him up Monday morning he could hardly move and they were not even aware of it. His fever was at 108 and he became non responsive. He could not even stand up.

They gave him oxygen and wrapped him in ice but by the time his fever went down he was brain dead. The owner was insensitive enough to tell us she wanted to buy us a new puppy (while standing over the body of our dead dog) as if our wonderful boy was replaceable.

Always check the conditions of where you board your pet.  The kennel in the back of this place used to be clean and well managed under the previous vet.  When I walked back there, it was appalling.  And apparently it appears our dog got an infection there and died under a doctors roof.       What a disgrace.

The staff here is very nice! I know my little BeBe is treated well here. 

They have a puppy package for $129, which includes all of the shots, flea preventative, worming, and a fecal test. Pretty nice. Since my poor little puppy had two types of worms, she had to get the actual medication for worms and some other things, so it was only $50 more. I know some people say it's so expensive and what not, but to me it's reasonable. I live sort of close to here, so it's easy to bring her to the vet as needed. 

The Dr. Shanima Salawan is very kind, and is to the point. She explains the plan, and at a reasonable price. Thank you guys!

Overall:
FRIENDLY, HELPFUL, AFFORDABLE, CONVENIENT!

I love this place! We started taking our furbabies here last year for deep teeth cleanings. We took two last year during the time they have the special & then this year we're bringing the other two. So I already did one about a week ago because they have the special now!!!! They do a great job & are so good with our furbaby!! I'm looking forward to bringing the last one!! I highly recommend Woodminster Veterinary for all your Furbabies needs!! They have great prices & a GREAT STAFF!!!!
