I wanted to find somewhere convenient and close to home but also a place where Dre would be comfortable. I believe we found that place. The front desk staff was very kind to me and most importantly Dre. I'm glad we found a place for him to get the treatment that he needs moving forward. Thank you.

Horrible service, no compassion whatsoever. Brought my dog in for a first time visit to get rabies shot, left without rabies shot. Apparently, they couldn't read THE DATES properly on my prior vaccination record from EBSPCA, said rabies was not needed. 
Since then have spent $$ for a dental, which was long overdue. Called today and still they maintain that rabies is not needed. I went line item by line item to prove that it was. Now I'm a new customer, there are coupons online for free rabies shot with initial exam (that I paid for already). Woodminster will not honor this coupon even though it was their mistake. Btw, first visit was less than two weeks ago. Bad practice, better off at SPCA.

We have continued to get great care at Woodminster Vet! They have been taking care of our two cats for about 5 years with routine check-ups​, as well as some UTI issues with one of our cats. They are very helpful over the phone when I have called needing advice, and try their best to squeeze you in if you need your pet to be seen right away. We also order and pick up prescription​ food with no issues. The best part is they never seem frazzled by my hissing cat, and have been able to take him in the back to give him shots when needed. Parking in the designated spaces in the lot or at a nearby meter is convenient​.
response_content: Woodminster Vet went above and beyond after reading my review and contacted me. I received an apologetic call where we discussed what went wrong. Seems like what happened was a communication mix up and they really wanted to fix what happened. They not only apologized, but they generously gave me some free cat food, which I never would have expected. This is the way to do business - you can tell they really care about their clients when something goes wrong. You have a new fan.

Message:
Woodminter Veterinary Hospital (Oakland CA) Has the best Doctor and Staff. They provide a vast variety of services. I have 3 dogs and one cat. I have been to alot of different Vet hospitals in the area but none of them were even comparable to Woodminter Vet Hospital. I was very pleased with there service and pricing. They were were very helpful ,caring and understanding towards my pets needs. Phone number is (510)531-0121

Came home to find my dog unable to open his left eye, and saturated with slimy gunk.  My friend recommended hot compresses for an hour.  Gave it a shot, and was able to get the eye open, but not all the way.  Thought I should get it checked out in case there was something in there I couldn't see.

These guys were able to take me in last minute on a saturday (strong bonus).  The admins/assistants were super friendly, and were very accomodating to my dog's sudden aversion to the vet office (strong sanitizer?).  

The vet seemed knowledgeable, and took him in the back to give him a dye test in order to see if his cornea was scratched.  Luckily it wasn't.  She then gave me eyedrops to administer. I'm just not entirely sure she gave the correct instructions for administration, as what she'd told me differed than what the insert said.  Also, the vet told me the drops were for pain.  My bf who happens to be a nurse actually recognized the product and told me they were for fungal infection (he actually had to use this type of medicine for his eyes previously) so...not sure I got the whole/accurate story on these meds. 

Another wierd thing was the vet wasn't very good at telling me what was going on.  She took my dog into the back, but I wasn't sure if I was supposed to follow her or wait in the room (she left the door open behind her), and she also emphasized how she'd administered the first dose of medicine (so I wouldn't think she'd given me a used bottle of meds?).  Just a little wierd.

Regardless, my pups eye was back to normal by the next day. I stopped using the drops altogether at that point, and he hasn't had any issues since.

I'd like to start by saying the girls at the front desk seemed knowledgable and friendly. The doctor however had a hard time making eye contact and my small dog was completely terrified of her, which is very strange because he loves women. 

The real issue is that they were too quick to jump to surgery. My 3yr old dog had a small growth on his lip, about the size of a grape, and the immediate solution was surgery...about $300-650 worth. When the assistant came in with the print out I asked, "Can't we atleast TRY some anti-biotics or something first before we put him under the knife?!?"

They insisted several times that the doctor didn't think it would do anything, but they sold them to me anyway. 

A week and a half later the growth had died and fallen off!! 

Now I know not every case is the same, but they should have taken some less severe precautions considering it didn't immediately seem like a life threatening situation. Every person I've talked to have all come to the same conclusion...they're just trying to make money.

I put this poor review on here to share our story in the hopes of preventing a shortened life of your best friend....

She's an indoor only, 6 year old black tabby. We knew something was wrong with our baby.  We took her to Woodminster a couple of times and told the vet something was wrong.  She was vomiting daily, seemed to have lost some weight, and seemed more lethargic than normal.  The vet kept saying "she looks great! everything is fine! her weight is perfect! she's very healthy!" and did some blood work on her and found nothing. 

Long story shortened: We knew something was wrong and decided to go to another vet.  Montclair Animal Hospital in Oakland understood our concern...  They performed an ultrasound the following day and found a tumor in her stomach.  Our baby has high grade lymphoma and has been undergoing chemotherapy at BAVS in San Leandro.  She is doing very well!  Montclair has even called us a couple of times to see how our baby is doing with her treatments.

Best vet yet! They always have been able to promptly get me an appointment and you can tell everyone that works there cares and has a genuine love of animals. I appreciated that treated my rescue dog who had been abused and was traumatized with special care when we got him neutered there. Definitely trust your pet to them!i took my cat( rip) there as well for years and they did there best to make him comfortable in his old age. 
I was in there once when this family bright in a stray that had been hit by a car and they were able to take great care of it and ended up helping them  to find him a home.

I've had the most personal follow-up care and support from Hannah at Woodminster, both with my previous dog several years ago, and with my new dog.  Both have had some issues with anesthesia and Hannah follows up with so much concern and time and care.  She is a gem and the reason I keep coming back!

We've been going to Woodminster Veterinary Hospital for the past 7 years. The staff have always been helpful and are wonderful with our dog. When we've had an emergency, they have taken us in right away. During Covid, they have been especially good at keeping the office going in a safe manner.

excellent care with my puppy.  This year I had a couple of emergencies with my puppy and they gave him the best attention, always with love and a lot of patience. Goffie is happy to have a veterinarian like woodminster.
response_content: I am very happy and grateful for the service and love that the guys of WOODMINSTER VET have given to my puppy which thanks to his care is now a healthy puppy, I am in love with the way they treat my puppy every time we visit the hospital. Thanks Woodminster for your services !!!!

review_text: I adored Woodminster Vet Hospital for their excellent service at a reasonable price. I've just had our two kittens there for our check ups and vaccines so far but they'll be going in again soon for their 1 year boosters. It's in a small quiet area of the East Bay so the location is perfect as well.

I discovered Woodminster Vet Hospital when I couldn't get a timely appointment at my previous vet's. I really needed to get my dog vaccinated before boarding him when I went on vacation, and Woodminster was able to fit me in. review_text:
Im very unhappy with them and I can tell you that they don't seem to care about losing customers.  Twice I have tried to get flea/tick medication refilled and both times they COMPLETELY ignore all of the requests as well as my phone calls. The first time it resulted in a flea infestation in our house. 

Both times 1800PetMeds sent them 3 faxes which they ignored. And both times I called them and left numerous messages.  Recently after 3 faxes were sent with no response, I called them and left messages for 2 days and said our dog is due for her Bravecto chew soon.  Again nobody calls me back after 3 days so I call them again & speak with a supervisor.  She tells me that they can't approve the refill because my dog is due for her annual checkup in one month, and Bravecto is a 3 month medication. If that's their policy then they should've bothered to tell us this back when we originally requested it! I wouldn't have even heard from them if I didn't call a third day in a row. What's worse is that the supervisor didn't even seem to care that their incompetence and negligence has caused us hardships... and now an added stressor during this pandemic.  

Needless to say we are finding a new vet clinic where the staff will be responsive and professional.  Considering their lack of accountability, I don't trust them anymore with my dog's health. However to try and accommodate you we offered two different types of flea prevention to be picked up same-day that work in the same manner as Bravecto, with the exception that they are monthly and not 90 days which would provide enough prevention until Lobo's annual exam was due. response_content:
Been a while since I've been in but I really owe this place a good review. I switched to this clinic after being referred here as I was told one of the vets had experience treating canine skin conditions. I had a senior Pomeranian at the time, with bad dermatitis. At the first check-up, Dr. Odar (sp?) asked about my dog's cough, which she'd had for her whole life, and which my previous vet clinic never asked about. A moment after listening to my dog's heartbeat, she informed me my pom had a heart murmur. In the ~10 years at our previous clinic, not once was this ever brought up. (Side note: I had access to a medical stethoscope at the time, and once I got home, I compared the heartbeats between my two dogs. One sounded like a normal ba-dum, ba-dum... And sure enough, my pom's heart had an odd 'whoosh' in it. I have zero medical background, and the difference was really f***ing obvious between the healthy heart and the unhealthy one :( So my old vet either never bothered to listen --in 10 years!-- to my dog's heart, or they weren't even competent enough to notice the problem. Since it was an ongoing condition that was never really addressed, I wrongly assumed it was not a serious condition.) Fortunately, Dr. Odar was able to prescribe a medicine to reduce my dog's cough and make her more comfortable. 
      The dermatitis treatment took some trial and error, but the vets at Woodminster seemed confident and capable, and it was not long before we found a suitable treatment for my dog. All the staff involved seemed genuinely concerned about my dog's health, and really made the whole experience as positive as it could be. To people concerned about price, yeah, it's expensive, but that's the medical field. Dentists are expensive. Doctors are expensive. We just don't usually pay out of pocket for those, and we usually do for our pets. My dog passed away a few years ago at the age of 13, but her last years were made comfortable by the staff at Woodminster, and for that I am still grateful. 
      More recently, I've taken in my other dog (a 15 y/o chihuahua mix) to get checked out for a physical and a lump on her leg. We worked with a new (to us) vet, Dr G, and he was also awesome. He had a mellow positive energy that didn't get my dog worked up, and was able to take care of everything as painlessly as possible. 

The short version: Consistently good experiences for ~4 years! :)

Up until January 15th, this place would have rated 5 stars from me. In the past, they have taken great care of my cats, and were sympathetic and helpful when I had to bring in my cat Whiskers for cremation, after a horrible illness. (They were able to get him over two months of a happy healthy life again, before his rapid decline)...

Anyway, after the fiasco with my cat Crunch this month, I don't think I'll be stepping foot inside of Woodminster ever again.
Crunch was an old (four months shy of his 16th birthday), healthy cat. He lost some weight over the years, but had no need for medications, other than his annual shots and a vitamin b-12 shot. Up until two days before he died, he was still eating, playing, and performing his 'dog tricks'. When he didn't eat one day, I took him to the vet the next day. 

Woodminster is expensive, but that is not my complaint; the fact that I spent $175.00 for a series of injections - without being told that those injections would only last for 24 hours - were a complete waste. If the injections had been explained to me in a thorough manner, I would have opted to have my buddy euthanized, holding him in my arms - instead of him dying an agonizing death the next evening (not to mention the trauma placed on my remaining three cats). 
As upset as I was, I knew that I had to wait a few days before calling them, so I wouldn't completely fall apart and go ape shit on them. The woman I spoke to was very sympathetic, but no offer of a refund, partial refund, a free service, etc was mentioned - not that I wanted or asked for one. I thought that I'd get a call back at least, from someone higher up the food chain...nothing. 
Hey - they got my money, so they must figure that there wasn't any need to say or do anything else. 

I plan on taking my buddy Crunch to the East Bay SPCA for cremation, instead of going to Woodminster. Hell - their price jumped from around $250 to $400 for cremation anyway.


Addendum  2/19/16:
 
I rec'd a surprise call over a week ago, from the owner with an apology of what happened. I told her more or less what I wrote in this review. She stated that they would be refunding the money I spent on Crunch, and I did in fact receive the check in yesterday's mail. 
Even though $175 won't take away the painful way in which Crunch died, Woodminster at least got some appreciation from me with the call, and one star back to my rate here on Yelp. I'm 50/50 as to whether I'll be going back though.

review_text: This was our first visit to Woodminster Vet Hospital, and I have to say that this is an excellent veterinary office with a small-town feel. Everyone here is great to deal with, and we felt that they really cared about us and our dog. I thought that the prices were really reasonable as well. The staff even followed up by phone to see if there were any questions or concerns after the appointment. I look forward to maintaining our dog's health with the staff at Woodminster.

After agreeing to meet with me about the ear cropping I had done, the vet was very kind and understanding about the situation and made every attempt to make it right. Very kind and professional, and i would recommend this to anyone wanting a good ear cropping for their dog.

Reviewing a veterinary clinic is tough, especially for someone like me with a dog that has perpetual seemingly un-curable skin problems. I have never found a veterinarian that was able to definitively tell me what is causing my dog's problems, and often I end up paying for numerous expensive tests that don't tell me much. 
That said the staff and veterinarians at Woodminster are a really nice group, and I particularly like Dr. Adar who I was referred to from another clinic as she has more knowledge about dog skin problems. 
At our first appointment Dr. Adar ran tests, and suggested giving our dog Comfortis in case he had a flea allergy (which he doesn't, but she wanted to make sure) the Comfortis did not help him, but Dr. Adar then gave us a prescription for Temaril P (steroids) to help our dog with his rashes, hives, redness, hair loss, hot spots and overwhelming itching. It immediately made a big difference! We were so relieved as we have tried everything, and I mean EVERYTHING to help our dog. 

There are a few reasons I don't give five stars: 
1) We had to take our dog in last year after he ate socks and then got very sick, the vet (not Dr. Adar) had us do a (very expensive) x-ray and then afterwards mentioned that the x-ray only finds hard objects - even though we knew our dog had eaten soft fabric socks and had told her as much. In the end they gave him fluids and anti-nausea medication and he passed the socks on his own, but we probably spent $1000 on that trip... 

2) There are several veterinarians that work at Woodminster and they all seem to also work at other offices so it seems like I see a different doctor each time I go in, which can be hard when you have to explain things all over again to a new doctor. 

3) Lack of communication - we had some miscommunication regarding our dog's prescription which resulted in him being off his meds for over a week, in the end it was worked out - but it was frustrating to deal with. 

Overall I do recommend Woodminster Veterinary Hospital, the staff is very sweet to my dog, and Dr. Adar is a good veterinarian. The office has good hours (open until 7pm on week days) which is great, and parking is easy.

We took our dog into Woodminster for a bad bout of vomiting and diarrhea.  They were very quick to immediately charge us over $700 for services before taking her back for tests.  They kept our dog in the back room for most of the afternoon for these tests, telling us she was doing great and taking fluids in the back room.

When we arrived to get her, we did not get to meet our normal vet (Dr. Adar).  Instead we received a consultation from the crazy Indian lady mentioned in other reviews.  We were immediately disappointed.   Her professional opinion was "I don't know what is wrong with her, you tell me", that we received after 20 painful minutes of her speaking for 30 seconds and then fluttering somewhere else in the office for two minutes without even telling us to wait a second.

Wait - we paid $700+ and didn't even get a recommendation on how to care for her after we left?  Yup.  The special flower of a doctor had fluttered off somewhere in the office at this point like it was a hidden camera joke of a TV show.  I learned more about my dog's condition through the internet and interpreting the results of her lab results than her professional advise of "you tell me what's wrong with her".

I am not expecting miracles - just more professional direction, and understanding that we just paid your office a significant amount of money.

This got worse when we got our sick one in the car.   She had three more bouts of diarrhea before we had made it the four miles home.  So - when we called to ask how she was doing, "Fine" was clearly a mixup for "she's in the back soiling herself as we speak".  When we got her home, the amount of poop in her fur made it clear that she had a miserable afternoon doing just that.  They had medicine, our permission to get her feeling better, but did not treat her or get her comfortable.

She was asked to come back for a follow up appointment, which they had the audacity to charge us for.  This was the first real vet experience we had received this incident with our normal vet, but it should have been at no cost - as all of our follow up visits have been at no cost.  We complained about the poor experience the day before but we still had to shell out more $$.

In summary - this is a value vet.  You won't get overcharged for service, but you may not get the service you want.  I am only rating this two stars because of Dr. Adar, but you'd better go to another establishment if you don't get her. 

We're transferring our records to a facility where we can get consistent care for our dog, and professional medical advice.  We are disappointed as we had such hope for this place, and decent/fair experiences up until now.

review_text:
IMHO Not for Doberman Pinchers.

When you Google "Ear Cropping," Woodminster Veterinary Hospital is at the top of Google's list. The ear cropping price starts at $179 for Pitbull dogs. However, if you have a dog other than a Pitbull, in my case a Doberman the price starts at $275. I was okay with that price as other vets are at $600 including medication and one visit, [On the average]. After all said and done we got out of the door spending $475, and that is with denying the blood work and bringing our own recovery cone from our previous Dobermans. What we received for $475 was pain meds, antibiotics, sedatives, and of course the ear cropping. I sucked it up and told myself I save about $100. The part that I did not get is how the Vet set the ears. My last five Doberman dogs had round backer rod wrapped in 4X4 gauze inserted in the dogs ear pockets then tapped up to beginning healing and training to stand up. This is where Vet totally screwed up, and that is putting politely.  When I received my dog from the ear cropping procedure his ears were tapped back, flat against his neck. So much his eye were bugging out.  The vet tech said to take the bandage off after 24 hours and message the ears. That was it! I am thinking to myself, is this a new procedures since my last Doberman had his ears cropped six years ago? I waited the 24 hours and then removed the bandage. My dogs ears were all crippled up, not looking good. I went into salvage mode and made post for my dog. When I previously dogs were picked up Vet for ear cropping, the Vet had already posted the ears. They would stay that way for a few weeks before new post were put in. Unfortunately, my dog had to go through some pain while I posted his ears, and that is with giving him pain meds. The Vets procedure may work for Pitbull dogs, I have never seen one cropped. The tack on fees and especially the ear cropping is defiantly NOT worth taking you Doberman to this Vet.

Where are we? Rural Texas?!), and we were in and out within 1 hr.

I've been to the whole gamut of veterinarians within the Bay Area. My dogs have needed to "go in" for reasons ranging from simply spay/neuter/shots to specialty services like oncology, cardiology, and orthopedic x-rays. I know what forking out $$$$ can get you, but I am also not Bill Gates and do not have an endless surplus of money to spend on veterinary bills. I do the best that I can for my dogs, given my financial means, and Woodminster is a veterinary hospital that reflects that mentality. Let's be real here. We all have our limitations. I will agree that the veterinarian here does not have fabulous social (and, therefore, business) skills. But let's remember that she's a one-woman practice. That is hard; it is physically/emotionally taxing, so I can understand why, at 7PM on a Friday, she'd look and act tired. But did she ever talk down to me? No, not at all. In fact, she took out her Ophthalmology book, showed me some diagrams/pictures, and showed me exactly what was going on with my little guy's eye. She was courteous and respectful of my choices; if I didn't want an extra service, I said "No" and she smiled/nodded and that was it. Easy peasy. 

Bottom line: they deliver solid and dependable services at EXTREMELY cheap prices. AND the secretary is super friendly, happy, and adorable! =) She bumps the review up to 5 stars.

I regret that it has taken me so long to write this review.  I want all my communities to know about what happened to my dog last April at Woodminster Veterinary Hospital's kennel in Oakland.

My sweet three-year-old cockapoo, Kazoo, was being boarded for five days at Woodminster over spring break while we were in San Diego.  When we dropped him off, he was a completely healthy dog who was given a clean bill of health from my veterinarian only two months earlier.  When my partner picked Kazoo up at the kennel, he knew immediately that something was seriously wrong.  A usually hyper dog, especially upon greeting us, Kazoo had virtually no energy.  The office staff told my partner that the veterinarian wanted to talk to him about a limp.  Instead, the veterinarian talked to him about dental issues.  There was no talk about the lack of energy (or even the limp).  When my partner brought Kazoo home, Kazoo began drinking lots of water and throwing up.  Since my partner was quite concerned, he called and reached me at the San Diego airport.  He suggested I speak with the veterinarian (Dr. Shanima Salwan) if possible.  When I spoke with Dr. Shanima by phone from the San Diego airport, she said that no one had noticed Kazoo having low energy.  

I returned home late that night and was very concerned about Kazoo's condition.  When I brought Kazoo to my veterinarian's office (Claremont Veterinary Hospital) first thing the next morning, he started to bleed from the tip of his penis and they found that he had a very low heart rate.  They decided to admit him for blood tests and life support.  He was bleeding internally and needed to be euthanized two days later.  The veterinarians at Claremont were very surprised by Kazoo's rapid deterioration and concluded that it was probably a result of either salmonella, a virus such as parvo (even though he had been vaccinated), or clostridium.  The veterinarian I spoke with said that he "most likely" contracted one of these illnesses while at Woodminster's kennel, either from being in unsanitary conditions, eating something rotten, or eating feces that contained disease.

I have been boarding dogs at Woodminster for quite awhile, but the place is under relatively new ownership by Dr. Shanima and her co-owners.  When I first visited Woodminster, when it was owned by the previous veterinarian, I was given a tour of the areas where the dogs stay.  A friend of mine who began boarding his dog at Woodminster under Dr. Shanima's ownership said that he asked for a tour and was denied.  Since Kazoo's death, I have done some research on Dr. Shanima and discovered that she used to work for American Animal Hospital in Fremont, an organization which has an unbelievable number of disturbing reviews on Yelp.

It has been difficult for me to write this review because the untimely death of Kazoo, whom we had since he was a nine-week-old puppy, was absolutely devastating to me and my family.  What made the circumstances of his passing additionally difficult was the flat-out denial by Dr. Shanima of anything even accidental having occurred while Kazoo was in their care.  I wanted to share Kazoo's story so that all of you who read this will consider carefully any decision to board your animals at Woodminster or take your pets to this veterinarian.  Although their price for boarding is much lower than most other kennels, you might wish to consider choosing a different kennel.
